newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican peso closes softer on U.S. rates, covering.
newsitem.headline: Mexican peso closes softer on U.S. rates, covering.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed soft on Thursday due to rising long-term U.S. interest rates and dollar demand by local and foreign brokers covering their dollar positions ahead of the weekend, traders said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 3.5 centavos weaker at 7.5260/7.5300 per dollar, and its 24-hour counterpart 0.7 of a cenatavo weaker at 7.5140/7.5190 per dollar.
"Many had short positions in dollars at the fixing rate...they had to sell them to cover themselves and this unleashed speculation against the peso," a trader said.

The fix is a peso-dollar rate calculated daily by the central bank that is used to settle some official peso-denominated transactions the following day. The fix for Friday was set today at 7.5052 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso weakened the most because dollars do not have to be paid for until Monday, allowing investors to keep the pesos over the weekend and invest them.
The peso was also hurt by worries that U.S. long bond rates could rise further on Friday after gains on Thursday.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond rate stood at 7.05 percent towards the close of peso trading in Mexico.
"The peso was too strong...due in part to corporations buying pesos to pay taxes yesterday, but the exchange rate was going to have to adjust sooner or later," said a trader.
The same-day peso closed earlier 0.7 of a centavo down at 7.4880/7.4920 per dollar.
